card.name: Small linking words in espionage passages
card.fires_on: Small linking words and punctuation (and, the, to, a comma, a quote mark) that sit right after an agency or place name, mostly in Cold War spy and history texts. The next word is usually another proper name.

modes.label: Linking word after an agency name
modes.description: "and", "the" or "to" right after CIA, KGB or a spy-related phrase.
modes.example: The duel between the CIA<< and>> the KGB, portrayed in countless books

modes.label: Comma or and inside a list of names
modes.description: A comma or "and" inside a list of cities or people, before the next item.
modes.example: he studied in the Jena, Halle<<,>> again Jena and Leipzig.

modes.label: Quote mark before a title
modes.description: An opening quote mark before a named agency in a legal passage.
modes.example: Federal law prohibits use of the words<< ">>Central Intelligence Agency," the initials "C

card.writes: No clear effect; it weakly suppresses security-related words and promotes odd name fragments.
card.plain: It fires on little connecting words that come right after the names of spy agencies or in lists of proper names.
